I have not completed the requested proof. In particular, I cannot responsibly state an exact value for the limit. The rigorous bounds I can establish are
\[
\boxed{\frac32\le
\liminf_{t\to\infty}\frac{\log b(t)}{\log t}
\le
\limsup_{t\to\infty}\frac{\log b(t)}{\log t}
\le2.}
\]
This is a gap in my solution, not a claim that the problem is open.

Here are the proofs and executable checks.

## 1. A lower bound

First, suppose an intersecting family \(\mathcal H\) is partitioned into \(s\) nonempty subfamilies with disjoint nonempty cores \(Y_1,\dots,Y_s\), and every member of subfamily \(i\) has at most \(r\) elements outside \(Y_i\). Then
\[
\tau(\mathcal H)\le (2r+1)(r+1). \tag{1}
\]

To prove this, choose a maximal collection
\[
H_{i_1},\dots,H_{i_m}
\]
from distinct subfamilies such that the residual sets
\[
R_j=H_{i_j}\setminus Y_{i_j}
\]
are pairwise disjoint.

For every pair \(a\ne b\), intersection of the original sets, disjointness of their cores, and disjointness of their residuals imply
\[
R_a\cap Y_{i_b}\ne\varnothing
\quad\text{or}\quad
R_b\cap Y_{i_a}\ne\varnothing.
\]
Each residual meets at most \(r\) disjoint cores. Consequently
\[
\binom m2\le mr,\qquad m\le2r+1.
\]
By maximality, every residual belonging to an unselected subfamily meets \(D=\bigcup_jR_j\). Thus \(D\), together with one point from each selected core, covers \(\mathcal H\). This proves (1).

Now consider any admissible instance in the question, and write
\[
a_i=k-|X_i|,\qquad B=\sum_i a_i.
\]
Choose \(s=\lceil t/2\rceil\) indices with the smallest \(a_i\). Their maximum residual size \(r\) satisfies
\[
r\le \frac{B}{t-s+1}\le\frac{2B}{t}.
\]
The union of these \(s\) subfamilies has covering number exactly \(s\): it has a cover consisting of one point from each of its cores, while a smaller cover, supplemented by one point from every other core, would cover the original family with fewer than \(t\) points.

Applying (1),
\[
\frac t2\le s\le(2r+1)(r+1)\le2(r+1)^2.
\]
Therefore
\[
B\ge \frac{t^{3/2}}4-\frac t2,
\]
and hence
\[
b(t)\ge \frac{t^{3/2}}4-\frac t2. \tag{2}
\]

## 2. An upper bound

Take pairwise disjoint blocks \(X_1,\dots,X_t\) with \(|X_i|=i\), and put \(k=t\). Define
\[
\mathcal F_i=
\left\{
X_i\cup\{x_{i+1},\dots,x_t\}:x_j\in X_j
\right\}.
\]
Every member has size \(t\). For \(i<j\), every member of \(\mathcal F_i\) meets \(X_j\), so it meets every member of \(\mathcal F_j\). Members of the same subfamily share their core.

One point from each block gives a cover of size \(t\). Conversely, let \(|C|\le t-1\), and let
\[
h=\max\{j:X_j\subseteq C\},
\]
taking \(h=0\) if there is no such block. Some block \(X_i\) with \(i>h\) is disjoint from \(C\): otherwise \(C\) would contain the \(h\) points of \(X_h\), when \(h>0\), and at least one point from every later block, requiring at least \(t\) points.

For every \(j>i\), choose \(x_j\in X_j\setminus C\), which is possible by the definition of \(h\). Then
\[
X_i\cup\{x_{i+1},\dots,x_t\}
\]
misses \(C\). Thus \(\tau(\mathcal F)=t\). The cost is
\[
\sum_{i=1}^t(t-i)=\binom t2,
\]
so
\[
b(t)\le\binom t2. \tag{3}
\]

Equations (2) and (3) give the displayed bounds on the logarithmic exponents.

## 3. Python checks actually run

The following checks the construction exhaustively for \(2\le t\le6\), including every potential cover of size \(t-1\). It also checks the residual-matching argument used in (1).

```python
from itertools import combinations, product
from math import comb

def construction(t):
    cores, p = [], 0
    for i in range(1, t + 1):
        cores.append(frozenset(range(p, p + i)))
        p += i

    groups = []
    for i in range(t):
        groups.append([
            cores[i] | frozenset(z)
            for z in product(*[tuple(X) for X in cores[i + 1:]])
        ])
    return cores, groups, p

def witness(cores, C):
    h = max(
        [i + 1 for i, X in enumerate(cores) if X <= C],
        default=0
    )
    i = next(
        i for i in range(h, len(cores))
        if not (cores[i] & C)
    )
    F = set(cores[i])
    for X in cores[i + 1:]:
        F.add(next(iter(X - C)))
    assert not (F & C)
    return i, frozenset(F)

def check_residual_matching(cores, groups):
    r = max(
        len(F - cores[i])
        for i, G in enumerate(groups) for F in G
    )
    D, chosen = set(), []

    for i, G in enumerate(groups):
        for F in G:
            R = F - cores[i]
            if D.isdisjoint(R):
                chosen.append((i, F, R))
                D.update(R)
                break

    m = len(chosen)
    for a, (i, F, R) in enumerate(chosen):
        for j, G, S in chosen[:a]:
            assert R.isdisjoint(S)
            assert F & G
            assert (R & cores[j]) or (S & cores[i])

    charges = sum(
        bool(R & cores[j])
        for i, F, R in chosen
        for j, G, S in chosen if i != j
    )
    assert comb(m, 2) <= charges <= m * r
    assert m <= 2 * r + 1

    cover = D | {
        next(iter(cores[i])) for i, F, R in chosen
    }
    assert all(cover & F for G in groups for F in G)
    assert len(cover) <= (2 * r + 1) * (r + 1)

for t in range(2, 7):
    cores, groups, n = construction(t)
    family = [F for G in groups for F in G]
    lookup = [set(G) for G in groups]

    assert len(family) == len(set(family))
    assert all(len(F) == t for F in family)
    assert all(
        not (cores[i] & cores[j])
        for i in range(t) for j in range(i)
    )
    assert all(
        cores[i] <= F
        for i, G in enumerate(groups) for F in G
    )
    assert all(
        F & G
        for i, F in enumerate(family) for G in family[:i]
    )

    tested = 0
    for c in combinations(range(n), t - 1):
        i, F = witness(cores, frozenset(c))
        assert F in lookup[i]
        tested += 1
    assert tested == comb(n, t - 1)

    cover = {next(iter(X)) for X in cores}
    assert all(cover & F for F in family)
    assert sum(t - len(X) for X in cores) == comb(t, 2)

    for bits in range(1, 1 << t):
        I = [i for i in range(t) if (bits >> i) & 1]
        check_residual_matching(
            [cores[i] for i in I],
            [groups[i] for i in I]
        )

    print(t, n, len(family), tested)
```
